title: Dominic and the Detention
premise: Wendell Whitlock, a debate champion drowning under his father's expectations, is paired for a semester project with Dominic Reyes, the detention-regular class clown who once humiliated him in front of the whole school. Forced together, they uncover that Wendell's father, a school board member, has been quietly funneling scholarship funds meant for students like Dominic into a private debate academy. As they build an unlikely partnership toward the state championship, Wendell must choose between exposing his father and protecting his own future. In the end, Wendell forfeits the final round to testify at the school board meeting, losing the trophy but winning something harder: his own voice, with Dominic standing beside him.
about_author: Vesper Nakamura is a former high school debater who spent four years collecting second-place trophies before discovering that the best arguments happen off the podium. They write stories about teenagers who learn that loyalty is a choice, not a debt.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He maps out the 147 days until graduation on his bedroom wall while rehearsing a debate case downstairs where his father critiques every word. Establishes the suffocating household and Wendell's coping strategy: perfect performance, zero honesty. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as ambition.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Ms. Okafor announces semester-long paired projects and reads the names: Whitlock and Reyes. The classroom goes silent; Dominic grins from the back row like he's won something. Wendell's carefully constructed invisibility shatters in one sentence. Emotional beat: humiliation resurfacing as anger.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He proposes meeting in detention—his natural habitat—and lays out rules: no questions about families, no mention of the incident freshman year. Wendell realizes Dominic remembers everything too. They split the work like a treaty between hostile nations. Emotional beat: wary truce masking old wounds.

chapters.title: Detention Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Afternoon sessions in Room 114 become routine: Wendell researches, Dominic jokes, and slowly real conversation leaks through. Wendell learns Dominic works nights to support his mother; Dominic learns Wendell's trophies are his father's, not his. Emotional beat: unexpected ease, guarded but growing.

chapters.title: The Incident, Retold
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He finally explains the freshman-year humiliation: he mocked Wendell's stutter during a practice round because his friends dared him, and he's regretted it since. Wendell doesn't forgive him, but hears him. The air between them changes weight. Emotional beat: confession without absolution.

chapters.title: Scholarship Season
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. While researching the project topic—educational equity—he stumbles on district budget documents showing the Reyes Scholarship Fund, founded by his grandfather, has been redirected to his father's private academy for three years. He closes the laptop and says nothing. Emotional beat: discovery curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Practice Round
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Wendell drags Dominic into debate practice as project 'field research,' and Dominic turns out to be a natural—quick, funny, devastating in cross-examination. The coach notices. Wendell feels something ugly and familiar: jealousy, inherited from his father. Emotional beat: admiration tangled with resentment.

chapters.title: Dinner at the Whitlocks'
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. His father invites Dominic to dinner as a 'case study' in underserved students, performing generosity while condescending to him. Dominic plays along brilliantly, then privately tells Wendell what he really saw: a man who treats his son like a product. Emotional beat: protective fury on Wendell's behalf.

chapters.title: The Fund
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Dominic discovers the scholarship was originally created for kids exactly like him—his middle school counselor nominated him the year it vanished. Wendell admits what he found weeks ago. Dominic's trust cracks; Wendell's silence becomes its own betrayal. Emotional beat: the first real rupture.

chapters.title: Silent Treatment
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Weeks of cold coexistence; the project stalls, the championship partnership dissolves, and Wendell wins a qualifier alone, feeling nothing. His father celebrates loudly. Wendell stares at his wall of days and realizes he's been counting down instead of living. Emotional beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: Room 114, Empty
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Ms. Okafor threatens to fail them both if the project isn't finished, forcing one last meeting. Instead of working, they finally fight—the incident, the fund, the silence—all of it. Exhausted, they say true things for the first time. Emotional beat: catharsis through collision.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. His father, sensing trouble, offers Wendell a deal: stay quiet about the fund, and the academy will guarantee his college admission and legacy. Wendell sees the machinery clearly for the first time—how his whole life has been purchased. Emotional beat: temptation offered plainly.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Case
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They rebuild the project together, this time around the real story: the stolen scholarship. Researching means interviewing families who lost funding, including Dominic's mother. Wendell learns to listen; Dominic learns to trust. Emotional beat: partnership reforged with purpose.

chapters.title: Qualifiers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They compete as a team for the first time and win the regional qualifier, earning a state championship berth. Celebrating afterward at a diner, Dominic asks the question Wendell dreads: what happens when the tournament ends and the truth begins? Emotional beat: joy shadowed by the coming choice.

chapters.title: Promposal Politics
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Prom approaches; classmates assume Wendell will go with his longtime debate partner Priya, but he realizes his feelings have shifted toward Dominic. A clumsy, half-joking promposal in Room 114 becomes real. Emotional beat: vulnerability beyond friendship.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Someone—an anonymous email to the student paper—exposes partial documents about the fund. Suspicion falls on both boys; Wendell's father accuses Dominic of theft and threatens expulsion. Wendell knows neither of them leaked it, but proving it means revealing what they know. Emotional beat: cornered.

chapters.title: Father's Son
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Confrontation at home: his father demands Wendell publicly distance himself from Dominic to save his reputation before states. Wendell, for the first time, refuses out loud. The argument he could never win, he stops trying to win—and simply walks out. Emotional beat: severance.

chapters.title: State Championship
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The final round arrives against the academy team funded by the stolen money. Mid-round, Wendell sets down his cards, addresses the judges, and forfeits—announcing why. The room erupts. They lose the title and win the story. Emotional beat: sacrifice as triumph.

chapters.title: Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell testifies before the school board with the full evidence, restoring the fund and naming his father's redirections. Dominic speaks too, not as a victim but as the scholarship's intended future. His father watches from the back and leaves early. Emotional beat: truth spoken without flinching.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Two days later, they show up to prom together—rumpled, exhausted, briefly famous. Priya saves them a table; even Ms. Okafor dances. For one night, nobody argues anything. Emotional beat: earned lightness.

chapters.title: One Hundred Forty-Six
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Graduation day. Wendell takes down his countdown wall and finds, behind the papers, the drawing eight-year-old Wendell made of what he wanted to be: not a champion—a person who tells the truth. He gives the speech his father would hate. Emotional beat: inheritance refused, self claimed.

chapters.title: After
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Summer begins. Dominic receives the restored scholarship letter addressed to him by name; Wendell packs for a state school his father didn't choose. They meet at Room 114's window one last time, then walk out the front doors together. Emotional beat: beginning, not ending.
